calc_concentracao.title: Spray Mixture Concentration Calculator
calc_concentracao.content:
[FAQ: What is the purpose of the Concentration Calculator?]
- Calculates the exact amount of pesticide to dilute per tank for Young Crop or Adult Canopy based on authorized DGAV label dosage.

[FAQ: What is Young Crop Mode?]
- Takes into account the target volume to prepare and recommended label concentration for early-stage crops.

[FAQ: What is Adult Canopy Mode?]
- Adjusts the calculation by integrating the recommended spray volume per hectare and actual volume applied by equipment.
calc_concentracao.unit_explanation:
Q_p : Pesticide Quantity (mL or g)
Volume : Liters (L)
Concentration : Percentage (%)

calc_dose.title: Dose Per Hectare Calculator
calc_dose.content:
[FAQ: What is the function of this calculator?]
- Converts label dose (L/ha or kg/ha) into exact product amount per tank based on calibrated spray volume.

[FAQ: How to calculate area covered per full tank?]
- Divide tank capacity by actual spray volume per hectare. Example: 1,000 L / 200 L/ha = 5.0 hectares per tank.
calc_dose.formula:
Q_p = (C_d × D × 1,000) / V_a
Area (ha) = C_d / V_a
calc_dose.unit_explanation:
Q_p : Product Quantity in Tank (mL or g)
C_d : Volume to Prepare (L)
D : Label Dose (L/ha or kg/ha)
V_a : Applied Volume (L/ha)

perfil_cultura.title: Crop Profile & Canopy Geometry
perfil_cultura.content:
[FAQ: Why record crop details?]
- Recording crop variety, phenological stage, and row spacing allows precise spray volume calculation and TRV adjustments.

[FAQ: What is Leaf Area Index (LAI)?]
- It is the ratio of total upper leaf surface area to ground surface area.
perfil_cultura.unit_explanation:
W_w : Row Spacing (m)
W : Canopy Width (m)
H : Canopy Height (m)

perfil_equipamento.title: Spraying Equipment Profile
perfil_equipamento.content:
[FAQ: Why record sprayer details?]
- Allows management of pump, filter, regulator, and tank specifications for ISO 16122 calibration tests.
perfil_equipamento.formula: Pump Flow Rate ≥ Total Flow Q_t + Agitation (≥5%)

perfil_bicos.title: Sprayer Nozzles Profile
perfil_bicos.content:
[FAQ: How does ISO nozzle classification work?]
- Nozzle color defines nominal flow rate at 3 bar pressure according to ISO 10625 standard.

[FAQ: Why does nozzle type matter?]
- Air-induction nozzles drastically reduce drift on windy days.
perfil_bicos.unit_explanation:
Q_nozzle : Nozzle Flow Rate (L/min)
Angle : Spray Angle (60°, 80°, 110°)

perfil_calibracao.title: Calibration Profile & Field Test
perfil_calibracao.content:
[FAQ: What is a calibration test?]
- A field test using clean water to determine real ground speed, nozzle flow rate, and spray volume applied per hectare.
perfil_calibracao.unit_explanation:
v : Speed (km/h)
Q_t : Total Flow Rate (L/min)
W_w : Working Width (m)

preferencias_unidades.title: Measurement Units & Standard Profiles
preferencias_unidades.content:
[FAQ: How do Unit Profiles work?]
- Allow switching between Metric (SI), US Customary, Anglo-Saxon, and Traditional Regional systems without losing hydraulic calculation precision.
preferencias_unidades.formula: Automatic conversion across DATERRA Smart ecosystem
preferencias_unidades.unit_explanation:
SI : L, ha, bar, km/h
US : gal, acre, psi, mph

calc_eppo.title: EPPO Calculator (LWA / TRV)
calc_eppo.content:
[FAQ: What is the function of the EPPO Calculator?]
- Calculates reference spray volume and plant protection product quantity per tank and per hectare based on vertical canopy area (LWA) or 3D canopy volume (TRV), adhering to the EPPO PP 1/239 standard.

[FAQ: What is the LWA (Leaf Wall Area) Method?]
- Measures vertical leaf wall area (m²/ha) in vineyards and hedge-grown crops.

[FAQ: What is the TRV (Tree Row Volume) Method?]
- Measures apparent tree canopy volume (m³/ha) in nut orchards, pome fruit, and citrus.
calc_eppo.formula:
LWA (m²/ha) = (2 × H × 10,000) / W_w
TRV (m³/ha) = (H × W × 10,000) / W_w
Spray Volume = LWA × (k_LWA / 10,000) or TRV × k_TRV
calc_eppo.unit_explanation:
H : Canopy/Foliage Height (m)
W : Canopy Width (m)
W_w : Row Spacing (m)
k_LWA : L/10,000m² LWA
k_TRV : L/m³ TRV

ajusteDose.heightTooltipVine: Use only the height of the canopy band actually being sprayed (e.g. bunch zone only), not total vine height. The target is the treated canopy.
ajusteDose.heightTooltipOrchard: Use only the height of the canopy band actually being sprayed (e.g. active tree foliar zone), not total tree height. The target is the treated canopy.
ajusteDose.lwaExplanation: LWA (Treated Leaf Wall Area): In hedgerow crops (vines and bush orchards), the target is the vertical treated area on both sides of the row: (2 x h x 10,000) / r. EPPO reference: 10,000 m²/ha.
ajusteDose.trvExplanation: TRV (Tree Row Volume): In orchards and globular canopy trees, the target is the three-dimensional tree volume: (h x w x SF x 10,000) / r. EPPO reference: 10,000 m³/ha.

guide.title: EPPO PP 1/239 Guide
guide.introHeading: 1 hectare of ground area does not equal 1 hectare of biological target.
guide.introBody: Two plots with the same ground area can have vastly different canopy volumes. Applying a "blind" dose based solely on surface area causes two critical problems: Overdosing in young orchards (financial waste, environmental pollution, and residue exceedance) and Underdosing in mature canopies (poor pest control and resistance development). The EPPO standard adjusts the dose to the actual canopy architecture.
guide.labelExpressionsSubtitle: On manufacturer documentation, recommended doses appear in 4 distinct expressions:
guide.dgaDesc: Traditional dose in L/ha or kg/ha. Assumes a "standard" crop stage. Must be adapted to your actual canopy.
guide.dlwaDesc: Dose expressed to treat 10,000 m² of treated leaf wall area.
guide.dtrvDesc: Dose expressed to treat 10,000 m³ of canopy tree row volume.
guide.dhlDesc: Product quantity to dilute per 100 Litres of water. Alone it does not determine rate per hectare; it always depends on sprayer water application volume.
guide.fieldVariablesTitle: 2. Field Variables (What to measure in the field?)
guide.varHDesc: The vertical canopy band actually targeted by spray nozzles (e.g. cluster zone). Not total plant height!
guide.varWDesc: Canopy thickness measured at mid-height of the treated zone (as width varies with height).
guide.varRDesc: Distance between the centre of one row and the centre of the adjacent row. Rule for bed/twin rows: Measure from the centre of one group to the centre of the next.
guide.varSfDesc: Volume correction factor for trees that deviate from a solid rectangular block (e.g. globular/rounded canopies).
guide.lwaBlockDesc: Treats the canopy as two vertical spraying walls. Ideal approach for continuous hedgerow systems (e.g. vineyards, trained fruit walls). Higher treated height or narrower spacing increases plot LWA.
guide.trvBlockDesc: Adds the 3rd dimension (width). Ideal method for globular tree canopies (e.g. freestanding fruit trees, citrus), determining 3D canopy volume per hectare.
guide.runoffRiskTitle: 4. Product Dose vs. Water Volume (Run-off Risk)
guide.runoffRiskDesc: The label prescribes the Dose (active ingredient quantity needed for protection). But Water Volume (the carrier volume) must be matched to sprayer nozzles and canopy density. Excess volume (e.g. washing leaves to the point of run-off, exceeding 1,000 L/ha unnecessarily) does not enhance efficacy; it washes active ingredient into the soil, causing run-off and crop protection loss.
guide.dssDesc: Application efficiency depends on sprayer technology (nozzle type, air assistance, droplet spectrum). To optimise both dose and spray volume without run-off, official DSS tools are recommended.
